questions.q: What does the Tsonga people's attitude toward kissing show?
a: A practice can vary by culture while love remains universal
Kissing is a universal sign of romantic love
Love is a Western idea rather than a human one
Monogamy exists in every known society
questions.why: The Tsonga find kissing strange, yet love still appears across cultures.

questions.q: Why was monogamy advantageous for society, according to the summary?
a: It gave each man a spouse and reduced the risk of men left alone
It increased genetic diversity within small groups
It strengthened alliances between neighboring tribes
It allowed women to inherit property and status
questions.why: Men without partners were more likely to turn to theft, violence and rape.

questions.q: How does the meaning of friendship differ between the US and Saudi Arabia?
a: Americans emphasize sharing feelings; Saudis treat physical contact as a sign
Americans value practical help; Saudis value formal titles
Americans prefer group activities; Saudis prefer solitude
Americans expect written commitments; Saudis rely on gifts
questions.why: Holding hands, normal between Saudi friends, looked strange to Americans.

questions.q: Why did friendship evolve, according to the summary?
a: Trusted groups helped each other survive without expecting a reward
It allowed early humans to compete for scarce mates
It developed only after the invention of agriculture
It helped people pass on their genes more quickly
questions.why: Early humans faced illness, hunger and weather better when they could rely on others.

questions.q: How does culture help humans survive in harsh environments?
a: It passes useful information and habits to the next generation
It eliminates the need for genetic adaptation
It prevents people from migrating to new regions
It makes every society behave in the same way
questions.why: Long lives and imitation let people inherit survival knowledge from their elders.
